title: Software Factory v0

repository.name: factory
repository.description: Software factory: dispatcher, runs and gates that turn approved Specs into reviewed pull requests

body:
## Problem Statement

I write and approve Specs, but implementing, reviewing and triaging them is hand-driven: I open a thread per issue, launch reviewer subagents myself, and chase unblocked work across thirteen repositories. I work nights and weekends, so work stops whenever I am away. I want to approve work and come back to reviewed pull requests, being pulled in only for decisions.

## Solution

A Factory: an hourly Dispatcher on homeserver2 finds Eligible work and launches Runs. Implementation Runs build a Ticket (or a whole Spec on one integration branch) test-first, pass a Gate, and open a pull request I merge. A Spec pipeline takes `needs-triage` issues, drafts and reviews a Spec, and hands it to me as `needs-spec-review` with its Open Decisions answered by recommendation. Anything that needs me becomes a label, a Follow-up Ticket, or, if urgent, a waiting thread.

## User Stories

1. As the owner, I want only my Approval (`ready-for-agent`) to start implementation, so that the Factory never builds something I have not endorsed.
2. As the owner, I want Tickets with open blockers skipped, so that work is never built on unfinished foundations.
3. As the owner, I want blocking edges across repositories honoured, so that a `cli` Ticket waits for its `sim-core` blocker.
4. As the owner, I want a Ticket claimed with a label and a titled thread, so that two Runs never work the same Ticket.
5. As the owner, I want a dead Run's Claim released after a Lease, so that a crash does not strand a Ticket forever.
6. As the owner, I want a Ticket handed to me after two failed attempts, so that retries cannot loop.
7. As the owner, I want a provider rate-limit retried with backoff without spending an attempt, so that a busy night does not mass-escalate Tickets.
8. As the owner, I want implementation by deepseek, Conformance Review by Sonnet 5.5 and Standards Review by Gemini 3.8 Flash, so that cheap implementation is checked by independent models.
9. As the owner, I want at most two review rounds, so that a stubborn disagreement reaches me instead of looping.
10. As the owner, I want a draft pull request with the findings when Gates keep failing, so that partial work is not lost.
11. As the owner, I want a spec-gap question posted on the issue with `needs-info`, so that I can answer it when I am back.
12. As the owner, I want human-only work filed as a `ready-for-human` Follow-up Ticket without holding up the pull request, so that code ships even when a secret needs setting.
13. As the owner, I want a Follow-up Ticket to block a dependent only when its body says why, so that blocking stays deliberate.
14. As the owner, I want a push notification only for an urgent Exit, so that I am not woken for ordinary work.
15. As the owner, I want a parent Spec's Approval to run all its Tickets on one integration branch, so that a chain costs me one merge.
16. As the owner, I want `needs-triage` issues turned into reviewed Spec drafts, so that I only review Specs.
17. As the owner, I want every drafted Spec to list its Open Decisions with recommended answers, so that I can approve by relabelling.
18. As the owner, I want only issues by org members or collaborators drafted, so that a stranger's text never reaches an unattended agent.
19. As the owner, I want a draft never to relabel itself `ready-for-agent` or `wontfix`, so that approval stays mine.
20. As the owner, I want launches to pause when my review queue is deep or the host is unhealthy, so that the Factory cannot bury me or starve homeserver2.
21. As the owner, I want one switch that stops everything, so that I can halt it instantly.
22. As the owner, I want a dry-run mode, so that I can read what it would do before it acts.
23. As the owner, I want a report three days after the first live Run, so that I can tune the Guards.
24. As the owner, I want a repository to join by adding one allowlist line, so that rollout is gradual.
25. As the owner, I want a repository's installed skills checked before a Run launches, so that a Run never starts without `implement`, `tdd` and `code-review`.

## Implementation Decisions

- The core is pure: given issues, blocking edges, labels, parent links, live threads, an allowlist and `now`, it returns decisions (launch, release, escalate, skip with a reason). All I/O sits in thin GitHub and T3 adapters. No clock and no randomness inside the core.
- Eligibility, reconciliation and each Guard are separate pure functions behind one decision interface; the Dispatcher composes them.
- State is read from labels, blocking edges, parent links and live threads only; the board Status column is written, never read (ADR 0001).
- A Spec Run uses `/implement-spec` on one integration branch; a Ticket Run uses `/implement` (ADR 0002).
- Role briefs for implementer, reviewers and Spec drafter are injected into each thread's launch prompt; they are not skills.
- Runs execute as the owner account on the host, repo-only by policy (infra ADR 0005).
- The Spec pipeline is a tiered loop: deepseek drafts, Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash critique for at most two rounds, Opus 5.5 adjudicates any remaining disagreement, then `needs-spec-review`.
- Guard thresholds start conservative and are tuned from the 3-day report (ADR 0003).
- The allowlist maps each repository to exactly one host. It starts with `sim-core`, `ledger-core`, `tax-core`, `cli`, `infra`, `technical-template`, all on homeserver2.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behaviour at one seam: the pure decision function. Inputs are fixtures of repository state; outputs are decisions with reasons.
- Adapters are tested against recorded GitHub and T3 responses, with a dry-run mode asserting that nothing is written.
- Prior art: the deterministic engines in `sim-core` and `ledger-core` (data in, data out).
- Scenario fixtures to cover: a blocked chain, a cross-repository blocker, a stale Claim, a rate-limited retry, a stranger-authored issue, a parent Spec with a mixed set of children.

## Out of Scope

- Merging pull requests, applying branch protection, creating repositories, or touching any host or cloud platform.
- homeserver1 execution (the allowlist supports it; enabling it is a later step).
- The GitHub webhook accelerator.
- Repositories outside the pilot allowlist, including `mcp-auth-gateway` and `agentic-inbox`.

## Further Notes

Built by hand with the existing `/implement` flow first; the Factory builds itself only once Ticket Runs work. The curated skill profile lives in `trajectonomics/internal-skills`, not here.
